grade.first_issue: No decisive defect; none of Rules A–F imposes a cap.
grade.summary: The submission gives a complete and correct proof. The nonnegative integer measures N and S never increase and at least one strictly decreases in every move, establishing termination and leaving exactly one entry greater than 1. Primewise, the gcd of all p-adic exponents is invariant under the Euclidean transformation (a,b) to (min(a,b),|a-b|), so the unique terminal integer is determined by the initial board.
strengths: Correctly computes the change in the total number of prime factors.
Correctly handles both gcd greater than 1 and coprime cases to prove termination.
Correctly proves that at least one entry greater than 1 always remains.
Identifies and proves the primewise exponent-gcd invariant.
Correctly reconstructs the terminal value as the product of primes raised to the invariant exponents.
